reason: As written the falsifier cannot discriminate. (1) Power: 2^20 steps, hit prob 2^{l-n}=2^{-ceil(n/2)}, so hits = 2^{20-ceil(n/2)} = 2048 at n=17 down to ~128 at n=25; relative sampling noise 2%..9% (more with walk autocorrelation) versus the stated null deviation O(2^{-n/2}) = 0.2%..0.02%. The null is ~10-400x below the noise floor, so 'frequency = 2^{l-n}(1+O(2^{-n/2}))' is untestable and 'excess grows with n' is confounded by noise that itself grows with n. Prediction_if_true is not quantified (no threshold, no test statistic). (2) Walk is redundant for the bias question: the r-adding walk is stationary on the (sub)group, so P(x(P) in V) equals |{P in E: x(P) in V}|/|E| exactly. That quantity is exactly computable by enumerating V (2^l elements, test Tr(x+a+b/x^2)=0, double count, add x=0 point) with no sampling noise. The walk only tests mixing, which is already covered by LEAD-RHO-r-adding-walk-mixing. (3) No null/control arm: needs random-hash-of-same-size control for the spectral part and a Gaussian/random-V null for the frequency part. (4) Wrong asymptotic expectation: for a random l-dim subspace the exact character-sum deviation is ~2^{-l/2} (square-root cancellation), relative to 2^{-n/4} at l=n/2, not 2^{-n/2}; l=n/2 sits at the edge of the Kohel-Shparlinski incomplete-sum range, so the stated prediction_if_false is not a theorem there. The informative statistic is the distribution of the normalised excess over V and its maximum over V (a sampler would pick the best V). (5) The 2^8 hashed quotient chain is not lumpable (image of a Markov chain under a non-lumpable map is not Markov), and with 2^20/2^8=4096 samples per row the empirical 256x256 matrix has a noise-floor second singular value ~0.06-0.1, which swamps any real V-correlated gap; without a hash-control the spectrum number is uninterpretable. (6) Runtime: n=17..25 odd is only 5 values (17,19,21,23,25), l=floor(n/2)=8..12. Pure-python GF(2^n) point addition (~50-150 us/step) x 2^20 x 5 n = 4-13 CPU-min if one walk is shared across the 8 subspaces, borderline; numpy log/antilog tables (2^25 int32 = 128MB at n=25) with many parallel walkers make it seconds. Exact enumeration of V costs 2^l <= 4096 field ops per V, negligible. (7) Metric is a structural quantity (frequency ratio, eigenvalue), not wall time: good. (8) Scaling to n=131: the toy says nothing about a gain at 131 by itself; it can only calibrate the exponent of the excess in l and n (fit log2|excess| vs l), which extrapolates the character-sum bound. Any measured excess is exponentially small in l, so at l large enough to matter (B=2^l factor base, l~40+) it is a constant-factor/engineering device and cannot get under B*D^2 << N; the experiment can confirm 'no advance' but not 'advance'. Idea retains a free, cheap, decisive kill, hence worth running in repaired form.
fix: Replace the sampled-frequency test with an exact one, add null arms, and keep the walk only for the mixing/spectral part. (A) Exact bias: for each odd n in {13,15,17,19,21,23,25,27,29} (curves y^2+xy=x^3+a x^2+b over F_2^n via gp ellinit on ffgen, or own numpy log tables) and each of >=200 random V of dim l in {floor(n/3), floor(n/2), ceil(2n/3)}, compute N_V=#{x in V: Tr(x+a+b/x^2)=0} (+x=0 point) by direct enumeration; define excess e_V = 2*N_V/|V|*... normalised as (#points with x in V)/(|V|) minus 1 (expected 1 for ratio |points|/|F|=1 up to Hasse). Null: same statistic on a random subset of F of size |V| (not a subspace) and on a random Z/2-linear-free set; compare the empirical sd of e_V to the predicted 2^{-l/2}. Report sd(e_V)*2^{l/2} (should be O(1) constant) and max_V e_V (hill-climb / random search over V to see whether optimised V gains more than sqrt(2 ln #V)*sd). Fit log2 sd vs l and n to extrapolate to l=40..65 at n=131; this is the scaling argument. Also test structured V (subfield-like, trace-orthogonal, V = span of low-weight vectors) which is where a bias could actually appear. (B) Walk part (cheap, optional): 5 curves x 2^22 steps (numpy vectorised, 64 parallel walkers, r=20, log tables) record class(x mod V) with class = hash of the coset of V to 256 buckets; control arm = identical hash applied to a random linear map F->F/V' with V' a different random subspace, and a shuffled-step-order control; statistic = second singular value of the empirical 256x256 count matrix normalised per row, compared to the row-count noise floor ~ 2/sqrt(count per row) and to the control arms; pre-register decision rule: reject 'V-correlated gap' if V arm lies within the control arms' 95% interval, and reject 'hitting bias' if |sd_V*2^{l/2} - 1| is within the null band. (C) Metrics reported are structural: excess ratio, eigenvalue, hit counts with CIs; no wall time. Budget: exact enumeration ~1 CPU-min total, walk part ~5-8 CPU-min with numpy. Pre-register that a positive result needs excess exceeding the random-V null by >5 sigma and growing as a fixed fraction of 2^{-l/2} rather than shrinking; otherwise close as 'engineering, constant factor, no advance'.
